  • Preservatives help prevent oxidation in food by slowing down or stopping the chemical reactions
  • between oxygen and food components like fats, oils, and vitamins. These reactions can cause:
  • Rancidity (bad smells and flavors), Color changes (like browning or fading), Nutrient loss
  • (especially of vitamins A, C, and E. Some preservatives act as antioxidants themselves (like
  • ascorbic acid or BHA) by:Binding oxygen before it can react with food, Neutralizing free radicals
  • that cause oxidative damage
